name: FirstUK Bank Escalation Matrix
description: The overarching operational framework for escalating issues within FirstUK Bank, managed by the Chief Operating Officer and the Operations department. It serves as a guide for all staff, management, and executives to handle operational risks and complaints.

name: Chief Operating Officer
description: The executive owner of the Escalation Matrix document, responsible for the overall governance of the escalation process.

name: Operations Department
description: The department responsible for the maintenance and execution of the escalation matrix procedures.

name: Escalation Matrix Process
description: A defined operational workflow that establishes clear paths for escalating issues, incidents, and decisions. The process is triggered based on severity, type, and financial impact to ensure rapid resolution and transparent accountability.
context: The Escalation Matrix defines clear escalation paths for issues, incidents, and decisions based on severity, type, and financial impact.
Ensures rapid resolution, appropriate authority, and transparent accountability.

name: Escalation and Approvals Procedure
description: A workflow defining the tiers of authority, approval limits, and response times for resolving customer issues and requests within FirstUK Bank.

name: Level 1 — Frontline Resolution
description: The first tier of resolution with an approval limit of less than £500 and a required response time of the same day (within 24 hours). It handles standard inquiries, simple fee reversals, and basic account maintenance.

name: Customer Service Staff
description: Frontline personnel authorized to handle Level 1 resolutions, including account inquiries and password resets.

name: Branch Staff
description: Frontline personnel authorized to handle Level 1 resolutions, including card replacements and fee reversals.

name: Account Managers
description: Frontline personnel authorized to handle Level 1 resolutions and standard product inquiries.

name: Account Inquiry Resolution
description: The action of resolving a customer's inquiry regarding their account at the frontline level.

name: Simple Fee Reversal Request
description: The process of requesting and approving the reversal of a bank fee, provided it is within the <£500 limit.

name: Standard Product Inquiry
description: Providing information to a customer regarding standard banking products.

name: Lost Card Replacement
description: The process of replacing a lost payment card, involving a $15 fee.

name: Password Reset
description: The action of resetting a customer's account password at the frontline level.

name: Level 2 Escalation Trigger
description: A decision gate where a case is moved from Level 1 to Level 2 if the customer remains unhappy or the issue is deemed too complex for frontline staff.
context: Escalation Condition: If customer unhappy or issue complex → Escalate to Level 2

name: Level 2 — Supervisor/Manager Resolution
description: A second-tier escalation level with an approval limit of £500–£5,000 and a target response time of 1–3 business days. It handles complaint investigations, non-standard fee reversals, and account exception handling.

name: Supervisor
description: An actor with authority to resolve issues at Level 2, including complaint investigations and fee reversals within the £500–£5,000 limit.
context: Authority: Supervisor, Branch Manager, Complaints Handler

name: Branch Manager
description: An actor with authority to resolve issues at Level 2, including complaint investigations and fee reversals within the £500–£5,000 limit.
context: Authority: Supervisor, Branch Manager, Complaints Handler

name: Complaints Handler
description: An actor with authority to resolve issues at Level 2, including complaint investigations and fee reversals within the £500–£5,000 limit.
context: Authority: Supervisor, Branch Manager, Complaints Handler

name: Level 2 Escalation Trigger
description: A decision gate to determine if a case remains at Level 2 or is escalated to Level 3 based on whether the issue is unresolved or has a financial impact exceeding £5,000.
context: Escalation Condition: If unresolved or >£5k impact → Escalate to Level 3

name: Complaint Investigation
description: A discrete action performed at Level 2 involving the investigation of a customer complaint.

name: Non-standard Fee Reversal
description: An action performed at Level 2 to reverse fees that do not fall under standard automated processes, subject to a £5,000 limit.

name: Account Exception Handling
description: A process step at Level 2 where account-related exceptions are managed by a supervisor or manager.

name: Customer Retention Offer
description: An action performed at Level 2 to provide offers to customers to prevent them from leaving the bank.

name: Process Waiver Request
description: A request handled at Level 2 to waive a standard operational process requirement.

name: Level 3 — Department Head Resolution
description: The third tier of the escalation matrix handled by the Department Head. This level manages high-value fraud investigations, regulatory exceptions, and high-risk AML/KYC decisions with an approval limit between £5,000 and £50,000 and a response time of 3–5 business days.

name: Department Head
description: The authoritative role responsible for resolving Level 3 escalations, including substantial refunds, regulatory exceptions, and high-risk customer decisions.
context: Authority: Department Head (e.g., Head of Retail Banking, Head of Compliance)

name: Level 3 Escalation Condition Gate
description: A decision point to determine if a matter can be resolved at Level 3 or must be moved to Level 4 based on whether the issue remains unresolved or the financial impact exceeds £50,000.
context: Escalation Condition: If unresolved or >£50k impact → Escalate to Level 4

name: Level 4 Escalation Tier
description: The subsequent escalation tier reached when Level 3 cannot resolve the issue or when the financial impact is greater than £50,000.

name: High-Risk Customer AML/KYC Decision Gate
description: A formal compliance gate where the Department Head makes a final determination on high-risk customer onboarding or maintenance following an AML/KYC escalation.

name: Level 4 — Executive Committee Resolution
description: The fourth tier of the escalation matrix managed by the Executive Committee. It handles high-impact issues ranging from £50,000 to £500,000 with a required response time of 24–48 hours.

name: Executive Committee
description: The governing body consisting of the CEO, CFO, CRO, and COO responsible for resolving major financial losses, regulatory breaches, and strategic exceptions.
context: Authority: CEO, CFO, CRO, COO (Executive Committee)

name: Level 4 Resolution Outcome Gate
description: A decision point to determine if the issue is resolved at the Executive Committee level or requires further escalation to the Board based on resolution status or a financial impact exceeding £500k.
context: Escalation Condition: If unresolved or >£500k impact → Escalate to Level 5 (Board)

name: Level 5 — Board Resolution
description: The final tier of escalation referred to when issues are unresolved by the Executive Committee or exceed a financial impact of £500,000.

name: Level 5 — Board Resolution
description: The highest tier of the escalation matrix, handled by the Board of Directors. It is triggered by major financial losses exceeding £500,000, critical regulatory breaches, or systemic operational failures, with a response time of 24–72 hours.
context: Response Time: 24–72 hours (emergency meeting if urgent)

name: Board of Directors
description: The governing body with the authority to resolve Level 5 escalations and approve financial limits exceeding £500,000.

name: Level 5 Escalation Trigger
description: A decision gate that determines if an issue must be escalated to the Board of Directors based on financial loss (>£500k), regulatory, reputational, or systemic risk.

name: Customer Complaints Escalation Process
description: A structured escalation workflow for handling customer complaints based on severity levels (Low, High, Critical), defining handlers, timelines, and regulatory notification requirements.

name: Customer Service Staff
description: The initial handler responsible for managing low-severity customer complaints within a 24-hour timeline.

name: Complaints Manager
description: An actor who serves as the escalation point for unresolved low-severity issues and the initial handler for high-severity complaints.

name: Head of Customer Service
description: A senior leader who acts as an initial handler for critical complaints involving regulatory or reputational breaches.
context: Initial Handler: Head of Customer Service + Compliance Head

name: Compliance Head
description: A senior officer who manages critical complaints and ensures regulatory notifications are handled.
context: Initial Handler: Head of Customer Service + Compliance Head

name: Compliance Team
description: The body notified when a high-severity complaint has regulatory implications.

name: Bank Board
description: The highest level of internal authority, notified of high-severity complaints exceeding £100k or critical breaches.

name: Financial Conduct Authority (FCA)
description: The external regulator that must be notified within 24 hours in the event of a critical regulatory or reputational breach.

name: Level 1–2 — Frontline Resolution
description: The initial tier of complaint handling managed by Customer Service Staff with a 24-hour resolution timeline.

name: Level 3 — Complaints Manager Resolution
description: The escalation tier for unresolved low-severity issues and the starting tier for high-severity issues.

name: Level 4 — Management Resolution
description: A high-level resolution tier involved in significant financial losses and critical breaches.

name: Level 5 — Executive/Board Resolution
description: The highest escalation tier for critical regulatory or reputational breaches involving the Board and Compliance Head.

name: Complaint Severity Assessment
description: The initial branching point where a complaint is categorized as Low, High, or Critical, determining the handler, timeline, and escalation path.

name: Low Severity Resolution Check
description: A decision point for low-severity complaints; if unresolved within 24 hours, the issue is escalated to Level 3.
context: If unresolved: Escalate to Complaints Manager (Level 3)

name: Financial Loss Threshold Check
description: A gate for high-severity complaints; if the financial loss exceeds £100k, the Board must be notified.

name: Fraud Incident Handling Process
description: An operational workflow for managing fraud incidents based on the monetary value of the fraud. The process defines different handlers, escalation levels, timelines, and mandatory actions depending on whether the amount is under £1,000, between £1,000–£10,000, or exceeds £10,000.

name: Fraud Amount Threshold Decision
description: A branching condition where the fraud incident path is determined by the financial value of the loss. The paths are split into three tiers: <£1,000, £1,000–£10,000, and >£10,000.

name: Financial Crime Team
description: The primary handler responsible for investigating fraud incidents under £10,000. For incidents between £1,000 and £10,000, they work in conjunction with the CRO.

name: Chief Risk Officer (CRO)
description: A senior actor involved in handling fraud incidents starting from £1,000. For incidents over £10,000, they act as a primary handler alongside the CEO.

name: Chief Executive Officer (CEO)
description: The highest level of management involved in the handling and investigation of high-value fraud incidents exceeding £10,000.

name: The Board
description: The governing body that must be updated when fraud incidents exceed £10,000.

name: Law Enforcement
description: External authorities contacted or notified for fraud incidents exceeding £1,000.

name: Level 2 — Financial Crime Team Resolution
description: The escalation tier for fraud incidents under £1,000, with a required resolution/action timeline of 24 hours.

name: Level 3 — Financial Crime Team and CRO Resolution
description: The escalation tier for fraud incidents between £1,000 and £10,000, requiring a 24-hour action timeline.

name: Level 4–5 — Executive Management Resolution
description: The highest escalation tier for fraud incidents exceeding £10,000, requiring an accelerated action timeline of 4 hours.

name: Fraud Investigation
description: The core action of examining the fraud incident to determine the cause and extent, required across all fraud amount tiers.

name: Account Block
description: The action of freezing or blocking an account to prevent further loss if the fraud is identified as ongoing, specifically for incidents under £1,000.

name: Customer Reimbursement
description: The process of returning funds to the customer. For amounts over £1,000, this must be completed within 10 days.

name: Law Enforcement Notification
description: The action of informing police or regulatory law enforcement agencies, warranted for incidents over £1,000.

name: Board Update
description: The formal communication of high-value fraud incidents (over £10,000) to the Bank's Board.

name: SAR Filing Compliance Check
description: A regulatory gate for incidents over £10,000 where it must be determined if a Suspicious Activity Report (SAR) is required for filing or notification.

name: Operational Incidents/System Outages Management Process
description: A workflow for managing system outages and operational incidents based on duration and customer impact. It defines specific handlers, escalation levels, and reporting requirements across three time-based tiers.

name: IT Operations
description: The primary technical handler responsible for resolving incidents with a duration of less than 4 hours.

name: Chief Technology Officer (CTO)
description: A senior actor involved in handling incidents lasting between 1 and 4 hours, and the primary handler for incidents exceeding 4 hours.

name: Chief Risk Officer (CRO)
description: An executive role that must be notified via escalation if an incident exceeds a 2-hour duration.
context: Escalate to CRO + COO after 2 hours

name: Chief Operating Officer (COO)
description: An executive role that must be notified via escalation if an incident exceeds a 2-hour duration.
context: Escalate to CRO + COO after 2 hours

name: Chief Executive Officer (CEO)
description: The highest-level handler responsible for critical incidents lasting more than 4 hours.

name: Executive Committee
description: The governing body that meets to review incidents that exceed a 4-hour duration.

name: Financial Conduct Authority (FCA)
description: The external regulatory body that may require notification for critical incidents lasting more than 4 hours.

name: The Board
description: The bank's board of directors, who must be updated if an incident duration exceeds 8 hours.

name: Level 1–2 — Initial IT Operations Resolution
description: The lowest escalation tier for minimal impact incidents lasting under 1 hour, handled by IT Operations.

name: Level 2–3 — IT Operations and CTO Resolution
description: The intermediate escalation tier for significant impact incidents lasting between 1 and 4 hours.

name: Level 4–5 — Executive Management Resolution
description: The highest escalation tier for critical impact incidents lasting more than 4 hours, involving the CTO and CEO.

name: Incident Duration Gate
description: A decision point based on the time elapsed since the incident start, determining the handler, escalation level, and reporting requirements (<1hr, 1-4hrs, >4hrs).

name: Executive Escalation Trigger (2 Hour Mark)
description: A trigger where the process escalates to the CRO and COO and initiates customer communication if the incident exceeds 2 hours.
context: Escalate to CRO + COO after 2 hours

name: Incident Logging
description: The act of recording the incident in the system, required for all incidents including those under 1 hour.
context: Log incident, no escalation if <1 hour

name: Customer Communication Update
description: The process of providing updates to customers when an incident exceeds 2 hours, or providing hourly updates for critical incidents over 4 hours.

name: Regulatory Notification Filing
description: The step of notifying the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) for critical incidents lasting more than 4 hours.

name: Compliance Violation Handling Process
description: A structured workflow for managing and remediating compliance violations based on severity levels. It defines specific handlers, timelines for corrective action, and reporting requirements ranging from internal counseling to regulatory notification.

name: Level 2 — Department Manager Resolution
description: The second tier of escalation for Policy Violations. It involves counseling and a corrective action plan to be implemented within 30 days.

name: Level 3 — CRO Remediation
description: The third tier of escalation for Low Impact Regulatory Rule Breaches. It requires immediate remediation within 5 days and internal notification.

name: Level 4–5 — Executive and Board Resolution
description: The highest tiers of escalation for Significant Regulatory Breaches. Requires immediate escalation and regulatory contact within 24 hours, including notification to the Board.

name: Compliance Team
description: Responsible for handling Policy Violations and Low Impact Regulatory Rule Breaches in coordination with management.

name: Department Manager
description: Jointly responsible with Compliance for handling Policy Violations and implementing corrective action plans.

name: Chief Risk Officer
description: Responsible for handling Low Impact Regulatory Rule Breaches and Significant Regulatory Breaches.

name: Chief Executive Officer
description: Responsible for the handling and escalation of Significant Regulatory Breaches.

name: Legal Department
description: Responsible for the handling of Significant Regulatory Breaches, particularly regarding regulatory contact and reporting.

name: Board
description: The governing body that must be immediately notified in the event of a Significant Regulatory Breach.

name: External Regulator
description: The external authority (FCA/PRA) to be notified in the event of a Significant Regulatory Breach.

name: Violation Severity Assessment
description: A decision point where a violation is categorized as either a Policy Violation, a Low Impact Regulatory Rule Breach, or a Significant Regulatory Breach to determine the handler and timeline.

name: Corrective Action Execution
description: The process of delivering counseling and implementing a corrective action plan within 30 days for policy violations.

name: Regulatory Remediation and Notification
description: Immediate remediation within 5 days for low impact breaches, including internal notification and documentation of the remediation.

name: Critical Regulatory Escalation
description: High-priority action for significant breaches involving regulatory contact within 24 hours and notification to the FCA/PRA.

name: Root Cause Analysis and Prevention Planning
description: A mandatory remediation step following a Significant Regulatory Breach to identify the cause and prevent recurrence.
context: Remediation: Root cause analysis + prevention plan

name: AML/KYC Issues Handling Process
description: An operational workflow for managing compliance failures and risks including missed KYC documentation, PEP/Sanctions hits, and suspicious transaction patterns. It defines handlers, escalation levels, and strict timelines for remediation and reporting.

name: Obtain Missing KYC Documentation
description: The action of retrieving missing KYC documents, which must be completed on the same day and prior to account processing.

name: Immediate Account Freeze
description: The immediate freezing of an account following a PEP or Sanctions hit, required to be executed within a 4-hour window.

name: NCA Notification
description: The process of notifying the Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation (OFSI) via the NCA following a PEP/Sanctions hit.
context: Reporting: NCA notification (Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation)

name: Enhanced Transaction Monitoring
description: The application of heightened monitoring to accounts exhibiting suspicious transaction patterns, with an investigation timeline of 5 days.

name: SAR Filing
description: The submission of a Suspicious Activity Report (SAR) if warranted by the investigation, to be completed within 30 days.

name: Compliance Team
description: The department responsible for handling missed KYC documentation and collaborating on Sanctions hits and suspicious patterns.

name: Financial Crime Team
description: The specialized unit responsible for managing PEP/Sanctions hits and investigating suspicious transaction patterns.

name: Level 2 Escalation
description: The escalation tier assigned to missed KYC documentation and the lower end of suspicious transaction pattern handling.

name: Level 3 Escalation
description: The escalation tier assigned to PEP/Sanctions hits and higher-risk suspicious transaction patterns.

name: Level 4 Escalation
description: The highest escalation tier cited, specifically for handling critical PEP or Sanctions hits.

name: KYC Documentation Check
description: A control gate to ensure all required KYC documentation is obtained before account processing can proceed.

name: PEP and Sanctions Screening Gate
description: A mandatory screening gate that triggers immediate account freezes and regulatory reporting upon a positive hit.

name: Decision Authority Matrix Process
description: A governance framework defining the financial limits and authority levels for approving various banking exceptions, reimbursements, and expenditures. It specifies the primary authority and the required escalation path based on monetary thresholds or risk factors.

name: Manager
description: An authority role responsible for approving fee reversals up to £1,000 and complaint resolutions up to £5,000.

name: Director
description: The escalation authority for fee reversals exceeding the £1,000 manager limit.

name: Chief Risk Officer (CRO)
description: A senior executive authority who handles escalations for complaint resolutions over £5,000, KYC exceptions involving PEPs or sanctions, and lending policy violations.

name: Compliance
description: The functional role responsible for approving fraud reimbursements up to £10,000.

name: Chief Executive Officer (CEO)
description: The highest level of authority for fraud reimbursements exceeding £10,000 and vendor contracts exceeding £100,000.

name: Compliance Head
description: The primary authority responsible for approving KYC Exceptions of any value.

name: Product Manager
description: The authority responsible for approving product exceptions up to £50,000.

name: Board
description: The governing body that provides approval for product exceptions exceeding £50,000.

name: Underwriter
description: The role responsible for lending exceptions provided they adhere to the credit policy.

name: Chief Technology Officer (CTO)
description: The authority responsible for approving system expenditure up to £50,000.

name: Chief Financial Officer (CFO)
description: The escalation authority for system expenditures exceeding £50,000.

name: Department Head
description: The authority responsible for signing vendor contracts up to £100,000.

name: Fee Reversal Authority Limit Check
description: A decision gate to determine if a fee reversal can be approved by a Manager (£1,000 limit) or must be escalated to a Director.

name: Complaint Resolution Authority Limit Check
description: A decision gate to determine if a complaint resolution can be approved by a Manager (£5,000 limit) or must be escalated to the CRO.

name: Fraud Reimbursement Authority Limit Check
description: A decision gate to determine if fraud reimbursement is within Compliance limits (£10,000) or requires CEO escalation.

name: KYC Exception Risk Gate
description: A decision gate where the Compliance Head approves standard exceptions, but PEP or sanctions-related exceptions are escalated to the CRO.
context: KYC Exception | Compliance Head | Any | CRO if PEP/sanctions

name: Product Exception Authority Limit Check
description: A decision gate determining if a product exception is within the Product Manager's £50,000 limit or requires Board approval.
context: Product Exception | Product Manager | £50,000 | Board if >£50k

name: Lending Policy Compliance Check
description: A check to see if a lending exception adheres to credit policy (approved by Underwriter) or violates it (escalated to CRO).
context: Lending Exception | Underwriter | Credit policy | CRO if policy violation

name: System Expenditure Authority Limit Check
description: A decision gate to check if system spend is within CTO limits (£50,000) or requires CFO escalation.

name: Vendor Contract Authority Limit Check
description: A decision gate to check if a vendor contract is within Department Head limits (£100,000) or requires CEO escalation.
context: Vendor Contract | Department Head | £100,000 | CEO if >£100k

name: Escalation Procedure
description: An operational workflow defining the criteria and triggers for escalating issues within the bank. It specifies conditions related to financial impact, regulatory risk, and timeframes that necessitate moving an issue to a higher authority.

name: Escalation Trigger Determination
description: A decision point where a staff member determines if an issue meets the criteria for immediate escalation. Triggers include exceeding approval limits, regulatory implications, reputational risk, or an issue remaining unresolved for 24 hours.
context: Financial impact exceeds your approval limit

name: Frontline Staff
description: The initial actor responsible for assessing whether an issue exceeds their specific approval limit or expertise, necessitating an escalation.
context: Financial impact exceeds your approval limit

name: Issue Escalation Process
description: A standardized operational workflow for documenting and escalating issues to the appropriate authority. It encompasses documentation, communication, decision implementation, and stakeholder notification.

name: Issue Documentation Step
description: The initial stage of escalation where the issue is formalized. It requires a summary, a timeline, an assessment of financial impact, and a record of efforts made so far.
context: Document Issue: Summary, timeline, financial impact, efforts so far

name: Contact Escalation Authority Step
description: The active communication phase where the actor contacts the escalation authority using both email and phone call without delay.
context: Contact Escalation Authority: Email + phone call (don't wait)

name: Escalation Authority
description: The individual or role responsible for reviewing escalated issues, asking clarifying questions, and providing a final decision for execution.

name: Provide Context Step
description: The phase where detailed background information is provided, including options that have been considered and a specific recommendation.
context: Provide Context: Background, options considered, recommendation

name: Response Awaiting Step
description: A waiting period where the actor must be prepared to respond promptly to any questions raised by the Escalation Authority.
context: Wait for Response: Authority may ask questions (respond promptly)

name: Authority Decision Point
description: The critical juncture where the Escalation Authority makes a determination on the issue, which then triggers immediate execution.

name: Decision Implementation Step
description: The execution phase where the decision rendered by the authority is put into immediate effect.
context: Implement Decision: Once authority decides, execute immediately

name: Stakeholder Update Step
description: The final stage of the process involving the notification of the customer, the internal team, and the manager regarding the outcome.
context: Update Stakeholders: Inform customer, team, manager

name: Customer
description: The bank customer who must be informed of the outcome following the decision and implementation of an escalated issue.

name: Manager
description: Internal leadership role that is notified once an escalated issue has been decided and implemented.

name: Escalation Procedure
description: A set of guidelines governing the etiquette and requirements for escalating operational issues to higher authorities. It focuses on the quality of context, the necessity of recommendations, and the adherence to decisions made by escalation authority.
context: provide complete context (don't make escalation authority investigate)
DON'T escalate until you've tried resolution at your level

name: Escalation Authority
description: The individual or body responsible for reviewing escalated issues, answering questions, and making final decisions. They require complete context and recommendations from the initiating staff.

name: Initiating Staff
description: The staff member responsible for attempting initial resolution and managing the escalation process. They must ensure they have exhausted their own authority limits before escalating.
context: DON'T escalate until you've tried resolution at your level
include recommendation (show you've thought it through)

name: Authority Limit Check
description: A decision gate used by staff to determine if an issue is trivial or within their own authority limit, thereby deciding whether an escalation is necessary.
context: DON'T escalate trivial issues (know your authority limit)
DON'T escalate until you've tried resolution at your level

name: Re-escalation Validity Check
description: A check to determine if an issue that has already been decided upon can be escalated again, triggered only if circumstances have changed.
context: DON'T escalate again if already decided (only if circumstances change)

name: Context and Recommendation Preparation
description: The action of assembling complete context and a reasoned recommendation before initiating an escalation to ensure the authority does not have to investigate from scratch.
context: provide complete context (don't make escalation authority investigate)
include recommendation (show you've thought it through)

name: Decision Implementation
description: The final step in the escalation workflow where the initiating staff implements the decision provided by the escalation authority without second-guessing.

name: Emergency Escalation Process
description: A 24/7 emergency escalation workflow used to resolve critical system, security, regulatory, or customer crises via on-call contacts. The process relies on a maintained On-Call List updated monthly by Operations.
context: On-Call List: Maintained by Operations, updated monthly

name: IT On-Call
description: The technical support actor responsible for responding to system outage escalations via the emergency phone line.

name: Security On-Call
description: The security response actor responsible for handling security incident escalations via the emergency phone line.

name: Chief Risk Officer (CRO)
description: The executive actor responsible for handling regulatory issues, contacted via a mobile number registered with the operations team.
context: Regulatory issue: Call CRO Mobile (registered with ops team)

name: CEO/COO
description: The highest level executive actors responsible for managing customer crises, contacted via numbers registered with the operations team.
context: Customer crisis: Call CEO/COO (registered with ops team)

name: Operations Team
description: The team responsible for maintaining and updating the On-Call List on a monthly basis.
context: On-Call List: Maintained by Operations, updated monthly

name: Emergency Type Classification
description: A branching point where the nature of the emergency (System, Security, Regulatory, or Customer) determines which on-call actor must be contacted.

name: On-Call List Maintenance
description: The recurring monthly action of updating the On-Call List to ensure current contact details for emergency responders are available.
context: On-Call List: Maintained by Operations, updated monthly

name: Level 1 Escalation
description: The first tier of the escalation matrix with the tightest turnaround times, requiring acknowledgment within 1 hour and same-day decisions.

name: Level 2 Escalation
description: The second tier of escalation requiring acknowledgment within 2 hours, a 2-day investigation period, and a decision within 3 days.

name: Level 3 Escalation
description: The third tier of escalation with a 4-hour acknowledgment window, a 3-day investigation period, and a 5-day decision timeline.

name: Level 4 Escalation
description: The fourth tier of escalation requiring acknowledgment within 2 hours, a 1-day investigation, and a decision within 2 days.

name: Level 5 Escalation
description: The fifth and highest tier of escalation requiring 1-hour acknowledgment and 24-hour investigation, with decisions typically taking 3 days unless critical, in which case they are immediate.
context: Level 5 | 1 hour | 24 hours | 3 days (or immediate if critical)

name: Escalation Reporting Process
description: The operational workflow for reporting and reviewing escalations on a monthly and quarterly basis. It includes tracking metrics such as resolution time and systemic issues, and notifying governance committees of high-level or regulatory escalations.

name: Monthly Escalation Report Generation
description: The monthly action of compiling escalation data, including total counts by level, average resolution times, common reasons, and trend analysis to identify systemic issues.

name: Quarterly Escalation Review
description: A quarterly governance activity where high-level escalations are reported to committees, trends are discussed, and process improvements are considered.

name: Board Risk Committee
description: The governance body responsible for being notified of Level 5 escalations during the quarterly review process.
context: Board Risk Committee notified of Level 5 escalations

name: Audit Committee
description: The oversight body responsible for being notified of regulatory escalations during the quarterly review process.
context: Audit committee notified of regulatory escalations

name: Level 5 Escalation
description: The highest tier of escalation requiring notification to the Board Risk Committee during the quarterly review.
context: Board Risk Committee notified of Level 5 escalations

name: Regulatory Escalation Check
description: A compliance gate ensuring that all escalations of a regulatory nature are identified and reported to the Audit Committee quarterly.
context: Audit committee notified of regulatory escalations

name: Chief Operating Officer
description: Executive authority responsible for the formal approval and sign-off of the operational procedure document.
context: Approved by: Chief Operating Officer — Date: 2026-01-15

name: Chief Executive Officer
description: Executive authority responsible for the final formal approval and sign-off of the operational procedure document.
